quarterly_data.signal: COO Manish Bhatia: Micron has more than 75% of its fiscal 2027 shipments committed, which 'shows a strengthening demand and allows us to shift our conversations on allocation with our customers out to 2028'; together with more SCA conversations (including an extension now negotiated) this gives 'very strong outlook for demand through 2028'. Supply growth stays structurally constrained: diminishing returns from technology transitions, HBM growing faster than conventional DRAM through 2028 (a rising share of industry output), higher trade ratios as the industry shifts from HBM3E to HBM4 and toward HBM4E late in 2027, and above all cleanroom space - even with first wafer output from Idaho mid-calendar 2027, meaningful supply growth takes a few quarters after a cleanroom opens. Bhatia: 'we really do not have line of sight to when supply and demand balances', and these are 'the reasons why we see that DRAM is reducing supply industry shipments next year'. CFO Mark Murphy: market conditions 'we would expect to remain tight, and that would be supportive through 2028'.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 75% of fiscal 2027 shipments committed; tight conditions expected through 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Mark Murphy on the outlook: the fiscal first-quarter guidance 'factors in a single-digit sequential bit growth, and double digit for cost for both DRAM and NAND'. For the balance of fiscal 2027 Micron had indicated margin expansion relative to Q1, a function of continued price increases 'albeit at a more moderate pace' plus a better product mix, partly offset by startup costs; Murphy expects to 'sustain strong financial performance'. Excluding incentive-comp effects, the year-over-year R&D increase will be more than the billion said last quarter: 'It will be over $1 billion in 2027 as we have added additional R&D activities.'
quarterly_data.figure: FQ1 guide: single-digit sequential bit growth for DRAM and NAND; FY2027 R&D increase over $1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Strategic Customer Agreements, per COO Manish Bhatia: since the last call Micron signed 10 new SCAs ('a range of agreements from small to large SCA customers'), for 26 in total, and now has SCAs across all business units including mobile and client. The SCAs cover both DRAM and NAND through 2030; Bhatia clarified, in bits, that 'the DRAM volume is a little bit less than that, approximately 35%, and the NAND bit volume is a little bit more', and said the share could go higher as SCA negotiations continue. About 3/4 of SCA revenue has a defined pricing framework and about 1/4 is open to periodic price negotiation with market dynamics; most pricing frameworks carry floor and ceiling bands, and the newer agreements are negotiated at current market conditions rather than the Q2 conditions of the earlier ones. Discussions with customers now extend commitments beyond 2030; Bhatia called the SCAs 'transformational for us in terms of being able to match supply with future demand'.
quarterly_data.figure: 10 new SCAs, 26 in total; through 2030 covering approximately 35% of DRAM bit volume (a little less) and a little more of NAND bit volume; about 3/4 of SCA revenue with a defined pricing framework, about 1/4 open to periodic negotiation

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Scott DeBoer: Micron has worked with NVIDIA for over a year on HBM4E, 'what's called NVHBM', which he expects to be 'the first major custom HBM product out in the market'. Unlike HBM4, which uses Micron's in-house base die, the HBM4E base die 'is on a foundry process, both for the customized product and for the, say, JEDEC specified product'. DeBoer says differentiation between suppliers comes in power, speed performance and product margin. COO Manish Bhatia expects NVHBM 'to be a high-value product'. Bhatia also said Micron increased HBM pricing significantly for calendar 2027, resetting at the start of the calendar year 'to narrow the profitability gap with conventional DRAM'; Micron is not updating its HBM TAM outlook and expects its HBM share to be around its broader DRAM market share without targeting one number.
quarterly_data.figure: HBM4E (NVHBM) co-designed with NVIDIA for over a year; HBM4E base die on a foundry process; HBM pricing increased significantly for calendar 2027

quarterly_data.signal: COO Manish Bhatia on capex: 'the principal constraint in the industry is on cleanroom space', and the majority of the fiscal 2027 construction capex increase versus prior plans is for cleanrooms that come online in late 2028 and beyond. CFO Mark Murphy: the majority of the increase is construction capex, mostly to accelerate cleanroom availability in 2028 and beyond, a trend he expects to continue beyond 2027; equipment goes in and wafers are produced 'when needed based on our view of the market'. Bhatia: Micron has been executing long-term supply agreements with equipment suppliers to secure access to equipment, but will equip the cleanrooms in line with demand trends at the time.
quarterly_data.figure: majority of the fiscal 2027 capex increase is construction capex for cleanrooms online in late 2028 and beyond

quarterly_data.signal: COO Manish Bhatia on CPU-driven demand: agentic workloads run across CPUs with 'a large attach rate of both LP as well as DDR memory and SSD', one reason server units are growing 'in the high teens', and this is 'making clear that DRAM is the principal constraint versus logic or power to the data center'. He says customers are maximizing compute silicon shipments with the memory supply available, creating latent demand: more memory, if available, 'would easily get put into use' in AI workloads attached to accelerators or CPUs.
quarterly_data.figure: server units growing in the high teens

quarterly_data.signal: CTO Scott DeBoer: Micron's technology leadership is 'at least two nodes ahead of the China competition'; 1-gamma DRAM is already the majority of Micron's bits and set to be the largest node in company history, and depends on EUV; the next node, 1-delta, is well underway with focus on its ramp 'in the second half of next year'. DeBoer says front-end process differences between DRAM optimized for HBM, SOCAMM, LPDRAM and GDDR6 on the same node are larger than ever; COO Manish Bhatia says running them on the same lines lets Micron flex mix to demand, though not necessarily lowering cost. Bhatia: China exposure has been falling and is expected to be in the single-digit range in fiscal 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: at least two nodes ahead of China competition; 1-delta ramp in the second half of next year; China exposure single-digit range in fiscal 2027

quarterly_data.signal: COO Manish Bhatia: the mobile and client business unit saw a sequential bit decline but revenue growth from higher pricing and favorable mix; premium client and flagship smartphone segments see robust demand for higher-content solutions, and Micron sees PC and mobile industry revenue growing even as unit volumes decline.

quarterly_data.signal: COO Manish Bhatia: Micron expects NAND conditions to be tight overall 'even as the industry is expected to grow in the mid-20% range in calendar 2027 and 2028'. Micron's NAND supply grew less than the industry this year because part of its Singapore cleanroom now hosts an advanced R&D line for future NAND and pilot HBM operations ahead of the HBM facility ramp in Singapore next year; continued ramp to G9 NAND is expected to give high-ROI, cost-effective supply, and the new cleanroom that broke ground earlier this year comes online in the second half of calendar 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: industry growth in the mid-20% range in calendar 2027 and 2028; new NAND cleanroom online in the second half of calendar 2028
